claim: Direct-five-cycle-count plan, full target subgoal: solved.
evidence: Set x=a_1 and y=a_2 in F_p^*. The recurrence successively gives a_3=(1+y)/x, a_4=(x+y+1)/(xy), a_5=(x+1)/y, a_6=x, a_7=y; admissibility justifies the cancellations and is equivalent to y!=-1, x+y+1!=0, x!=-1. Thus sequences are in bijection with pairs in (F_p^*)^2 outside A={y=-1}, B={x=-1}, C={x+y+1=0}. Their sizes are p-1,p-1,p-2. Only A and B intersect, in one point, so the bad union has size 3p-5. Hence F(p)=(p-1)^2-(3p-5)=(p-2)(p-3). For p mod 5 equal to 1,2,3,4, this product is respectively 2,0,0,2 mod 5.
